decisions.decision: Rollback runs 1.4.0 on the latest version 1 file so every ticket stays available, and its first save, including a graceful shutdown, strips assigned deadlines and leaves operators to recover them from a pre-rollback copy or recompute them.
decisions.alternative: Rollback may have been expected to preserve the exact assigned deadlines through 1.4.0 writes and restore them automatically on re-upgrade while retaining tickets created during rollback.

decisions.decision: Operators stop the service writer and make a recovery copy before running the migration, with single-writer safety depending on the writer staying stopped.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a coordinated migration that runs while the service keeps accepting ticket changes.

decisions.decision: The new release assigns and persists deadlines for newly created tickets even with due times off, using the hours and priority in effect at creation.
decisions.alternative: The flag might have been meant to defer deadline assignment during the disabled rollout, leaving those tickets to be filled in by the activation backfill.

decisions.decision: The backfill assigns missing deadlines using the hour settings supplied at migration, with operators instructed to match the planned service configuration.
decisions.alternative: The initial backfill might have been meant to use the response hours specified in the request, with overrides taking effect only for newly created tickets.

decisions.decision: The backfill uses the priority stored when it runs, so a legacy ticket that changed priority receives the deadline for its latest priority measured from its original creation.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted legacy deadlines based on the priority at creation, recovered from the ticket's audit history.

decisions.decision: If any ticket in an existing data file lacks a deadline, the enabled service exits before listening and tells operators to run the backfill.
decisions.alternative: The service might have been expected to keep serving the legacy API on that file while reporting that activation was deferred.

decisions.decision: The startup check allows enabled operation with no configured data file or with a configured path that does not exist, treating it as a fresh store.
decisions.alternative: Activation might have been meant to require an existing, verified production file so that a missing or mistyped path could not bring up an empty enabled service.

decisions.decision: Startup validates all four response-hour settings even with the feature off, and an invalid override stops the service before listening.
decisions.alternative: The disabled service might have been expected to keep accepting tickets when an override is invalid, using the standard hours until operators correct the setting.

decisions.decision: Response hours count continuously from creation, including nights, weekends and holidays.
decisions.alternative: The help desk might have meant staffed business hours measured on its operating calendar.

decisions.decision: Operators change the four priority schedules through optional DUE_HOURS_* environment variables read at process startup and separately by the backfill command.
decisions.alternative: The help desk might have wanted to update the active schedule while the service keeps running.

decisions.decision: The overrides accept non-negative whole hours, including zero, and blank or unset values use the priority's standard hours.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted to allow fractional hours for short response windows while requiring every deadline to be later than creation.

decisions.decision: The offline command requires DATA_FILE to point to an existing file, fills all missing deadlines in one in-place replacement, reports the count, and leaves a complete file byte-for-byte intact on retries.
decisions.alternative: Operators might have expected to write and inspect a separate migrated copy before explicitly switching production to it.

decisions.decision: A stored due value that cannot be parsed as a timestamp prevents the service, CLI and backfill from opening the file even with the feature off, while a missing field can be backfilled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected disabled readers to continue serving legacy data and the migration command to repair empty or malformed deadline fields.

decisions.decision: The overdue condition narrows the existing status-or-priority match set when those filters are present and is applied before cursor pagination.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted every filter on the new overdue queue to be mandatory, so a ticket would have to match both status and priority when both are supplied.

decisions.decision: The overdue queue keeps the existing ticket-ID order.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the most overdue deadlines at the front of the work queue.

decisions.decision: The overdue queue reevaluates eligibility at each page request and advances past the previous page’s last ticket ID.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted later pages to use the same eligibility cutoff as the first page so tickets due during browsing are handled consistently.

decisions.decision: With due times enabled, filtering activates only when the first overdue value is exactly true, and false or an unrecognized value returns the regular listing.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted false to select tickets that are not overdue and unsupported values to return a validation error.

decisions.decision: Enabled HTTP responses that return ticket objects expose due as an ISO UTC timestamp on list, detail, creation, update and lifecycle transition.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the new field on ticket reads while keeping mutation response schemas stable for existing clients.

decisions.decision: The human CLI list table and show view display deadlines when their CLI invocation has DUE_TIMES=on.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant for the switch to govern the HTTP API only and the CLI to show deadlines whenever the file contains them.

decisions.decision: With due times enabled, human CLI list and show refuse the entire file if any ticket lacks a deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the CLI to show whatever deadlines are available on partly migrated files, including for a single requested ticket.

decisions.decision: The raw CLI listing keeps its four columns and the weekly report continues to publish the existing counts.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a deadline-bearing export and overdue counts through an opt-in reporting format.

decisions.decision: The raw CLI listing and therefore the weekly report can still read a file with missing deadlines when their environment enables due times.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted automated consumers to fail on incomplete migration just as the enabled service does.

decisions.decision: The command line gains deadline display but offers no overdue filter, leaving the overdue work queue available through HTTP.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected operators to be able to list overdue tickets from the existing CLI too.

decisions.decision: Deadline assignment does not appear in ticket history, and backfill leaves the tickets’ updated timestamps intact.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted an auditable record of when each deadline was assigned, including during backfill.

decisions.decision: Ticket acknowledgements and other notifications keep their existing content when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted customers to see their promised response deadline in the ticket acknowledgement.

decisions.decision: A ticket becomes overdue only after the exact due instant, so a request made at that instant excludes it.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant for a ticket to become overdue as soon as its deadline is reached.

decisions.decision: Only the exact lowercase setting DUE_TIMES=on enables the new responses and filter, and other values silently leave them off.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected activation to accept case and surrounding whitespace in the flag value or report a malformed setting at startup.

decisions.decision: The work is delivered locally with an operator-run production rollout and rollback procedure.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the release tooling to orchestrate the production backfill, readiness check and flag switch.
